artifacts.summary: Live-run-verified triage of all 3 named defects in run-all.sh: Defect 1's per-suite [FAIL] naming is already shipped (task 261, 2026-09-25) and only the end-of-run roster is missing; Defect 2's baseline manifest is genuinely absent (the existing prose list in shell-script-testing.md is stale, missing 2 of 8 live failures); root-caused 3 of 8 failures to one shared stale-fixture bug (missing lib/return-meta-status-vocabulary.sh in three suites' hardcoded sandbox copy-lists), 2 to real unrelated repo defects (Gate 20 budget drift, a JSON-channel-discipline violation), 1 to an uncommitted WIP edit elsewhere in the repo, 1 to a distinct real aggregation bug, and 1 to the already-documented ambient-load flake; Defect 3's wall-clock highest-leverage fix identified is passing --skip-slow to orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's deploy_findings_snapshot() calls, which re-run the full 105-suite Gate 8 battery 2-3x per cycle.

memory_candidates.content: When a shell-test suite builds a synthetic sandbox by copying a hardcoded list of collaborator lib/*.sh filenames (rather than globbing lib/*.sh), the list silently drifts stale whenever the real script under test gains a new lib dependency, causing every case to fail identically with a 'shared library not found' error that looks like a logic regression but is a fixture-maintenance gap. Check git blame on the SUT's dependency-loading block against the suite's own copy-list age before assuming a red test describes a real defect.

orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's redeploy checkpoint calls lib/deploy-baseline-lib.sh's deploy_findings_snapshot() 2-3x per cycle (pre/post/confirm), each running the full verify-deploy.sh --findings --quiet with no --skip-slow or --only-gate, i.e. re-running the entire ~105-suite Gate 8 shell-test battery 2-3 times per cycle on top of whatever the dispatched agent already ran as its own phase gate. This is the concrete mechanism behind orchestration wall-clock complaints about run-all.sh being invoked repeatedly in one dispatch.

run-all.sh's [FAIL] <suite path> line is deliberately unprefixed (unlike [RUN]/[PASS]/[SKIP], which carry a '[run-all] ' prefix and are suppressed by --quiet). A caller or human grepping for the '[run-all] ' prefix pattern consistently will find zero FAIL lines even though the harness has emitted the per-suite failure-naming contract since 2026-09-25 (task 261 phase 6.1) -- verify current source/behavior with a live run before trusting a described symptom about this harness's output.
